_notes: Down off the roofs into the Shambles and Needle Lane. The gutter-wisp teaches Shadow, and the night starts being wrong.
Scenes 6-11 of the prologue as it was before the split; `--scene story:<index>` still counts across the whole prologue, not within this file.

scenes.art_desc: Looking down from the roofs into the sleeping Shambles at night: stalls shut under canvas, one lit lantern, and a thread of silver light stretched between two chimneys. Ash on the ridge, bare-necked — this is before the collar.
lines: Below: the Shambles, shut for the night, stalls sleeping under canvas.
Eight bells from the tower, the whole count, one to eight, dropped into the fog like coins into a well. There used to be a ninth. Nobody remembers when that changed, and nobody finds it strange.
And between two chimneys, strung across the dark like a hair caught in a comb: a thread of silver light. Humming.

Everything alive trails a thread, if you have the eyes for it. They run out of windows and along gutters, wound around wrists and doorposts and gateposts. Witches stitch with them. Cats only see them.
Hers I know by heart: silver, with a particular twist to it, like handwriting. This one is silver too, and it is nobody's I know.
I did not chase it. A cat of my age, carrying a gift, does not go haring off after every unexplained glimmer. The lie I told myself about not wanting to weighed nothing at all. Almost nothing.
Street level, Needle Lane, and the fog rolls up from the Mere to meet me. The shadows deepen, deep enough to wear, if you know how. I have been a rumor most of my life.
Something small and hungry climbs out of the gutter. A GUTTER-WISP: a swallowed lantern of a thing, all glow and appetite.
They eat small lies, and the city breathes out enough of those to keep a great many of them fed. This one heard mine. It has come to collect.

notes: ❋ SHADOW, the black energy. It hides and it wards — and in this fog it costs one less.

coach.text: Every fight opens with the going-in. STALK spends 2 Shadow straight off the spool and starts you unseen — or walk in and spend nothing.
This is your hand: ENERGY, not actions. You spend it to power the things you do.

text_by_approach.stalk: Two Shadow came off the spool for the entrance — an approach is paid off the spool, never from your hand. This is your hand: ENERGY, not actions.
text_by_approach.walk_in: You spent nothing to get in — spool and hand both untouched. This is ENERGY, not actions — you feed it to the things you do.
text_by_approach.ambush: Two Ferocity came off the spool for the entrance. This is your hand: ENERGY, not actions.
text_by_approach.case: Two Guile came off the spool for the entrance, and it bought you a longer look. This is your hand: ENERGY, not actions.
text_by_approach.ward: Two Moonlight came off the spool for the entrance. This is your hand: ENERGY, not actions.

coach.text: Every place has a rule. In this fog, Shadow costs one less — so SLINK is free here.
Read the chip up top: it tells you the next move BEFORE it happens. Some moves take HEALTH. Some take a card out of your HAND.
SLINK: guard 3. The fog makes it free — but it has 3 USES, and uses do not come back until Ash sleeps at home. Tonight, 3 is all you get.
Three guard, until this turn ends. It will soak a bite. It will NOT stop a theft — for that, spend the card: energy already fed onto an action cannot be stolen.
POUNCE carried over from the roof with 2 uses left. Charges are a whole night's budget, not a per-fight one — they refill when Ash sleeps at home, and nowhere else.
When you have nothing left worth doing, END TURN — the night moves too. Or stay: there is a free Scratch in the tray and energy in your hand. It is your turn.

lines: A cat and a lit appetite had a disagreement in a foggy gutter. The fog was on my side. The wisp went back down the drain, dimmer.
I sat longer than I meant to afterward, putting my coat back in order.
I let it keep its opinions and its drain. There is no arguing with weather made of appetite.
I sat longer than I meant to afterward, and told myself I was being thorough.
